label: thm:separable
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:separable}
The resonance variety of each hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ is strongly isotropic.
head: environment

title: Lemma
head: environment

label: def:cent
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:cent}
The \emph{centralizer} of a subspace $P\subseteq V^{\vee}$ is defined as 
\[
\operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(P)\coloneqq \bigcap_{p\in P} \operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(p)
=\bigl\{g\in V^{\vee}: p\wedge g\in I^2(\mathcal{A})\ \text{for all}\ p\in P\bigr\}.
\]
head: environment

label: lem:rigidity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:rigidity}
Let $P\subseteq V^{\vee}$ be an isotropic subspace with $\dim P\ge 2$. Then $P$ is maximal among the isotropic subspaces of $V^{\vee}$ if and only if $\operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(P)=P$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume first that $P$ is maximal among the isotropic subspaces of $V^{\vee}$.
Since $P$ is isotropic, we have $P\subseteq \operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(P)$. Suppose there exists $g\in \operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(P)\setminus P$. If we consider $P':=P+\mathbb C\cdot g$, then for all $p,p'\in P$ and all $\lambda,\mu\in \mathbb{C}$, we obtain
\[
(p+\lambda g)\wedge (p'+\mu g)=p\wedge p'+\mu\, p\wedge g-\lambda\, p'\wedge g
\in I^2(\mathcal{A}).
\]
This implies that $P'$ is isotropic, contradicting the maximality of $P$.

Conversely, assume $\operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(P)=P$ and let $P'\supseteq P$ be isotropic. For every $g\in P'$ and every $p\in P\subseteq P'$ we have $p\wedge g\in\bigwedge^2P'\subseteq I^2(\mathcal{A})$, so $g\in\operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(P)=P$, and hence $P'=P$ and $P$ is maximal.

label: thm:multinet-spaces
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:multinet-spaces} Notation as above.

\noindent (1) Each space $P_{\mathcal{N}}$ in \eqref{eq:PN} is an isotropic subspace of $V^\vee$ contained in $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{A})$.

\noindent (2) Every positive-dimensional irreducible component $P$ of $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{A})$ is a linear subspace, and $P=P_{\mathcal{N}}$ for some multinet $\mathcal{N}$ on a subarrangement.                                                 
Moreover, every positive-dimensional irreducible component of $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{A})$ is maximal among the isotropic subspaces of $V^{\vee}$.

label: eq:parXp=0
title: Proof
body_md:
We write a general element $p\in P$ as $p=\sum_i \lambda_i u_i\in P$, with $\sum_i \lambda_i=0$. In particular,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:parXp=0}
 \partial_X(p) = \sum_i \lambda_i \partial_X(u_i)=n_X \sum_i \lambda_i = 0\text{ for every }X\in \mathcal{X}.
\end{equation}
Suppose first that $g\in \operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(P)$.  If $X\in\mathcal{X}$ then using \eqref{eq:X-from-B_i} we can find block indices $i\neq j$ such that $X$ meets $\mathcal{B}_i$ and $\mathcal{B}_j$, so $(u_i)_X\neq 0\neq (u_j)_X$. Taking $p=u_i-u_j$ we have $p_X\neq 0$ and $\partial_X(p)=0$, while \eqref{eq:local-to-global} implies that $p_X\wedge g_X\in I^2(\mathcal{A}_X)$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:local-wedge}\ref{lw2}, we conclude that $g$ satisfies \ref{C1}. If $Y\in L_2(\mathcal{A})\setminus \mathcal{X}$ meets $\mathcal{B}_i$ then $(u_i)_Y\neq 0$ and using Definition~\ref{def:multinet}\eqref{m2}, $Y$ meets no other block. Taking $p=u_i-u_j$ for some $j\neq i$, we get $p_Y=(u_i)_Y\neq 0$, and $\partial_Y (p)=\partial_Y (u_i)=\sum_{H\in \mathcal{B}_i,\, Y\subseteq H} m_H>0$. Applying \eqref{eq:local-to-global} again implies $p_Y\wedge g_Y\in I^2(\mathcal{A}_Y)$, and therefore Lemma~\ref{lem:local-wedge}\ref{lw1} shows that $g$ satisfies \ref{C2}.

\vskip 4pt

For the reverse implication, if we assume $g$ satisfies \ref{C1} and \ref{C2}, it suffices by \eqref{eq:local-to-global} to check that $p_Y\wedge g_Y\in I^2(\mathcal{A}_Y)$ for all $p\in P$ and $Y\in L_2(\mathcal{A})$. If $X\in\mathcal{X}$ then \eqref{eq:parXp=0}, \ref{C1}, and \eqref{eq:wedge-criterion} imply $p_X\wedge g_X\in I^2(\mathcal{A}_X)$. If $Y\in L_2(\mathcal{A})\setminus \mathcal{X}$ meets some block $\mathcal{B}_i$ then this block is unique, hence either $p_Y=\lambda_i(u_i)_Y$ or $g_Y$ is proportional to $p_Y$ by \ref{C2}, proving $p_Y\wedge g_Y=0$. If $Y$ meets no $\mathcal{B}_i$ then $p_Y=0$ and we have again $p_Y\wedge g_Y=0$, concluding the proof.
head: environment

label: lem:outside
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
To prove \eqref{eq:allbase} for $L\in\mathcal{B}_i$, we suppose by contradiction that $Y=H\cap L\not\in\mathcal{X}$. It follows that $g_Y=c\,(u_i)_Y$ for some scalar $c$, and since $g_H\neq 0$ we get $(u_i)_H\neq 0$. This forces $H\in\mathcal{B}_i$, contradicting the assumption $H\in\mathcal{A}\setminus\mathcal{B}$.

Consider now a general block index $j$. A hyperplane $L\in\mathcal{B}_j$ contains at most one flat $X\in\mathcal{X}$ with $X\subset H$ (otherwise we would have $L=H$, but $H\not\in\mathcal{B}$) and therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq:double-sum-XinXXandH}
\sum_{X\in \mathcal{X},\, X\subset H} n_X
=\sum_{\substack{L\in \mathcal{B}_j\\ L\cap H\in \mathcal{X}}} m_L
\le \sum_{L\in \mathcal{B}_j} m_L=d .
\end{equation}
Moreover, equality holds in \eqref{eq:double-sum-XinXXandH} for $j=i$ because the condition $L\cap H\in \mathcal{X}$ holds for $L\in\mathcal{B}_i$. Since the two sides of \eqref{eq:double-sum-XinXXandH} are independent of $j$, equality must in fact hold for all $j$. Since $m_L>0$ for $L\in\mathcal{B}_j$, we conclude that $L\cap H\in\mathcal{X}$ for all $L\in\mathcal{B}_j$, as desired.
head: environment

label: lem:blockwise
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:incidence-system
title: Proof
body_md:
Set $\mathcal{O}:=\{H\in \mathcal{A}\setminus \mathcal{B}: g_H\ne 0\}$, then let $g_j\in \mathbb{C}^{\mathcal{B}_j}$ and $g_{\mathcal{O}}\in \mathbb{C}^{\mathcal{O}}$ be the corresponding coordinate columns of $g$, and let ${\bf{M}}$ be the $\lvert\mathcal{X}\rvert\times \lvert\mathcal{O}\rvert$ incidence matrix defined by $M_{X,H}=1$ if $X\subseteq H$ and $M_{X,H}=0$ otherwise. The equations $\partial_X g=0$, for $X\in \mathcal{X}$, assemble into the identity
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:incidence-system}
{\bf{J}}_1g_1+\cdots+{\bf{J}}_kg_k+{\bf{M}}g_{\mathcal{O}}=0  \in \mathbb{C}^{\mathcal{X}}.
\end{equation}
Fix a block index $j$. If $h\ne j$, then any $H\in \mathcal{B}_j$ and $L\in \mathcal{B}_h$ determine a unique base-point $H\cap L\in\mathcal{X}$, by Definition~\ref{def:multinet}\eqref{m2}. It follows that ${\bf{J}}_j^{T}{\bf{J}}_h={\bf{E}}_{jh}$ is the $\lvert\mathcal{B}_j\rvert\times \lvert\mathcal{B}_h\rvert$ matrix, having all entries equal to $1$. Likewise,
the condition \eqref{eq:allbase} implies ${\bf{J}}_j^{T}{\bf{M}}={\bf{E}}_{j\mathcal{O}}$, this being the $\lvert\mathcal{B}_j\rvert\times \lvert\mathcal{O}\rvert$ matrix having all entries equal to $1$. Writing
$s_h=\sum_{L\in \mathcal{B}_h}g_L$ and $s_{\mathcal{O}}=\sum_{H\in \mathcal{O}}g_H$ and multiplying \eqref{eq:incidence-system} by ${\bf{J}}_j^{T}$, we obtain
\[
{\bf{J}}_j^{T}{\bf{J}}_jg_j+\Bigl(\sum_{h\ne j}s_h+s_O\Bigr)\mathbf{1}_j=0 .
\]
The equation $\partial g=0$ implies $\sum_h s_h+s_{\mathcal{O}}=0$, so $\sum_{h\ne j}s_h+s_O=-s_j$.
Since ${\bf{E}}_jg_j=s_j\mathbf{1}_j$, it follows that ${\bf{Q}}_jg_j=\bigl({\bf{J}}_j^{T}{\bf{J}}_j-{\bf{E}}_j\bigr)g_j=0$, and \eqref{eq:kerQ} implies $g_j\in \mathbb{C} m_j$, which yields \eqref{eq:proportional}.
head: environment

label: prop:propagation
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In order to prove that $g\in \operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(P_{\mathcal{N}})$, we verify that $g$ satisfies the conditions from Proposition \ref{prop:cent-local}. Note that condition \ref{C1} is the same as \ref{P2}, so it suffices to verify \ref{C2}.

\vskip 4pt

Combining \ref{P3} and Lemma \ref{lem:outside}, it follows that every $H\in \mathcal{A}\setminus \mathcal{B}$ with $g_H\ne 0$
satisfies \eqref{eq:allbase}. Using \ref{P1}, \ref{P2} and Lemma~\ref{lem:blockwise}, we can find scalars $c_1,\cdots,c_k$ such that \eqref{eq:proportional} holds.

\vskip 4pt

To check \ref{C2}, we consider $Y\in L_2(\mathcal{A})\setminus\mathcal{X}$ meeting a block $\mathcal{B}_j$ and proceed to proving that $g_Y = c_j(u_j)_Y$. Since $g_H=c_j m_H$ for $H\in\mathcal{B}_j$, it suffices to prove that $g_H=0$ when $Y\subset H$ and $H\not\in\mathcal{B}_j$. Suppose that there exists such $H$ with $g_H\neq 0$. Since $Y$ meets no block of $\mathcal{B}$ different from $\mathcal{B}_j$ (by \eqref{eq:X-from-B_i}), we can further assume that $H\in
\mathcal{A}\setminus\mathcal{B}$. Since $Y$ meets $\mathcal{B}_j$, there exists $L\in\mathcal{B}_j$ such that $Y\subset L$, and \eqref{eq:allbase} implies that $Y=H\cap L\in\mathcal{X}$, a contradiction.
head: environment

label: eq:omega-normal
title: Proof
body_md:
The inclusion $\supseteq$ follows from Definition \ref{def:cent}, so it suffices to verify the inclusion $\subseteq$. We let $\omega\in \bigl(P\wedge V^{\vee}\bigr)\cap I^2(\mathcal{A})$ and write, using the basis
\eqref{eq:PN},
\[
\omega=\sum_{i=2}^{k}(u_i-u_1)\wedge h_i , \qquad h_i\in V^{\vee}.
\]
Set $g_i\coloneqq h_i$ for $i\ge 2$ and $g_1\coloneqq -\sum_{i=2}^k h_i$, to obtain the more symmetric representation
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:omega-normal}
\omega=\sum_{i=1}^{k} u_i\wedge g_i\qquad\text{where}\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{k} g_i=0.
\end{equation}

With this notation, we verify the hypotheses \ref{P1}--\ref{P3} of Proposition \ref{prop:propagation} for $g=g_i$, for each block index $i=1, \ldots, k$.

\medskip

\noindent\emph{Condition \ref{P1}.} Since $\omega\in I^2(\mathcal{A})\subseteq \ker \partial$ and
$\partial u_i=d$ for every $i$, applying $\partial$ to \eqref{eq:omega-normal} yields
\[
0=\partial \omega=\sum_{i=1}^k\bigl(d\, g_i-(\partial g_i)u_i\bigr)=d\sum_{i=1}^k g_i -\sum_{i=1}^k (\partial g_i)\, u_i
\overset{\eqref{eq:omega-normal}}{=}-\sum_{i=1}^k (\partial g_i)\, u_i.
\]
Since the vectors $u_i$ are linearly independent, it follows that $\partial g_i=0$ for all $i$.

\medskip

\noindent\emph{Condition \ref{P2}.} Decomposing $\omega$ with respect to \eqref{eq:brieskorn}, we get $\omega_X=\sum_i (u_i)_X\wedge (g_i)_X\in I^2(\mathcal{A}_X)$, and $\partial_X \omega_X=0$. If $X\in \mathcal{X}$ then $\partial_X u_i=n_X$ and therefore
\[
0=\partial_X\omega_X
=n_X\sum_{i=1}^k (g_i)_X-\sum_{i=1}^k (\partial_X g_i)\,(u_i)_X \overset{\eqref{eq:omega-normal}}{=} -\sum_{i=1}^k (\partial_X g_i)\,(u_i)_X.
\]
The vectors $(u_i)_X$ are non-zero with pairwise
disjoint supports, hence $\partial_X g_i=0$ for all $i$.

\medskip

\noindent\emph{Condition \ref{P3}.} Suppose that
$Y\in L_2(\mathcal{A})\setminus \mathcal{X}$ meets the block $\mathcal{B}_i$. By Definition~\ref{def:multinet}\eqref{m2} no other block can meet $Y$, so
$(u_l)_Y=0$ for $l\ne i$ and therefore
$\omega_Y=(u_i)_Y\wedge (g_i)_Y\in I^2(\mathcal{A}_Y)$. Since
$\partial_Y (u_i)=\sum_{H\in \mathcal{B}_i,\, Y\subseteq H}m_H>0$,
Lemma \ref{lem:local-wedge}\ref{lw1} implies that $(g_i)_Y$ is proportional to $(u_i)_Y$.

\medskip

We can therefore apply Proposition \ref{prop:propagation} to conclude that $g_i\in \operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(P)$ for every $i$. In
particular $h_i=g_i\in \operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(P)$ for $i\ge 2$, hence
$\omega=\sum_{i\ge 2}(u_i-u_1)\wedge h_i\in P\wedge \operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(P)$.

label: cor:separable-maximal
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: By Theorem~\ref{thm:multinet-spaces}, $P_{\mathcal{N}}$ is isotropic of dimension $\geq 2$. Lemma \ref{lem:rigidity} and the maximality of $P_{\mathcal{N}}$ implies that $P_{\mathcal{N}}=\operatorname{Cent}_{\mathcal{A}}(P_{\mathcal{N}})$. Separability of $P_{\mathcal{N}}$ follows then from Theorem~\ref{thm:factorization}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let $P$ denote a positive--dimensional irreducible component of $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{A})$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:multinet-spaces}, $P=P_{\mathcal{N}}$ as in \eqref{eq:PN} and it is isotropic. The conclusion then follows from Corollary~\ref{cor:separable-maximal}.
